facts.text: The Formosan black bear lives in the mountain forests of Taiwan and has a well-known white V-shaped mark on its chest.
Reported encounters between people and Formosan black bears have become more frequent in recent years.
Acorns are a favorite food of the bears in autumn.
The bears are alert and secretive, with a keen sense of smell and good hearing, and usually leave as soon as they detect people.
Food smells left by hikers may draw bears into forests where people are active.
Park staff have found bear tracks and fresh claw marks near park trails.
Bears are not hunting targets, but they are caught by accident in steel snares set for deer and wild boar.
Snares that tighten as a bear struggles can break bones or cut off paws or toes.
Hunters and farmers have been given new snares, free of charge, that are designed to catch only smaller animals.
People who report bears caught in traps can receive a reward.
Hikers are advised to bring a bear bell and a whistle to make noise and to travel in groups rather than alone.
Visitors are advised not to hike in the early morning or at dusk.
Hikers should seal food waste and carry all trash and food out, because leftovers may attract bears.
Anyone who sees a bear should stay calm, not take photos, and leave quietly and quickly.
Mother bears are protective of their cubs and may see people as a threat, so hikers should be extra careful around cubs.
If a bear comes toward you, do not run, scream, or turn your back; back away slowly.
Hikers are asked to report bear sightings and signs of bears to park stations.
